subject: trekkies
one_liner: An encrypted messenger that stamps every message in stardates, fact-checks it against canon, and delays delivery for realism.
brand_voice_notes: Talks like a ship's operations officer reading a quarterly report aloud. Treats canon disputes as compliance incidents and family members as pre-warp civilizations. Never winks. Never names a franchise. Assumes the reader already owns the uniform.

hero.sub: Subspace is the encrypted messenger for people with opinions about warp cores. Every message is stardate-stamped, canon-checked and delayed by the correct transmission lag before it reaches the rest of the crew.

features.title: Stardate timestamps
features.blurb: Every message is stamped using four competing stardate formulas, displayed side by side. Nobody in the chat knows what time it is. Our research shows this was already the case.

features.title: Canon Enforcement
features.blurb: A bot reads every message and posts a correction within four seconds if anything contradicts established continuity. It also corrects its own corrections. One thread in our beta reached 9,400 replies and is still open.

features.title: Prime Directive filter
features.blurb: Messages from non-fans are delivered, marked read and never answered. Subspace gently reminds you not to interfere with their development. Most users enable it for their in-laws on day one.

testimonials.quote: I texted my sister happy birthday in March. Canon Enforcement has been correcting it ever since. She has not replied, which the app tells me is the Prime Directive working.
testimonials.name: Dale Oberholtzer
testimonials.title: Regional Claims Adjuster and Self-Appointed Chief Engineer, Toledo Away Team

testimonials.quote: Our group chat has 41,000 messages about whether the transporter kills you. Subspace is the first app that let us pin all of them.
testimonials.name: Priya Venkataraman
testimonials.title: Senior Payroll Specialist, Former Convention Panel Moderator (Asked Not to Return)

testimonials.quote: The Prime Directive filter muted my husband during dinner. We have not argued since. We have also not spoken. The crew is functioning normally.

testimonials.title: Conlang Tutor (Level 2, Certified), Married 22 Years

demo_screen_concept: A three-pane desktop messenger styled as a starship console. Left rail lists channels (Toledo Away Team, Transporter Ethics, Mom, Captain's Log) with unread counts and a Prime Directive shield on non-fan contacts. The centre pane is the Toledo Away Team thread: messages carry a stardate in four formats, a Canon Enforcement bot replies inline with corrections, and a composer that canon-checks your draft live and flags violations before sending. Sent messages sit in a 'transmitting' state for a subspace lag you set with a slider in the right panel. The right panel also holds the Prime Directive toggle (collapses messages from non-fans into a 'non-interference' strip), a stardate format switcher, and a 'Hail' button that opens a viewscreen modal where the call never connects.

design_direction.style: Retro-futurist starship console, bridge night mode. A messaging app's landing page built like a 1980s-imagined ship operations panel: deep space-navy ground, rounded 'elbow' panel frames that wrap sections like console bezels, flat fills in amber, peach, lavender and rose, tall condensed uppercase labels, and monospace telemetry readouts. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: clay tubes, stash blobs, deploy pills, nap meters, ticket stubs, perforations, seat codes, fee stacks, queue strips, race bibs, split clocks, pace lines, motion slants, trail signs, blazes, contour lines, label tape, crossed-out names, middle slots, fridge magnets, ghost text, keycaps, squiggles, chrome bubbles, read receipts, sale-bill stacks, lot boxes, manicules, misregistration. Also absent: serif type, paper textures, glassmorphism, hard offset shadows, drop shadows, daylight backgrounds. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The elbow frame: every section sits inside an L-shaped coloured bezel with a fat rounded outer corner and a thin top bar, section label set inside the bar. (2) The telemetry readout: tiny mono numeric codes beside every heading ('04-1931 · DECK 7'), the only decoration. (3) The stardate stamp: four stardate formats stacked under testimonials and chat messages, all disagreeing. (4) The pill button stack: CTAs and tier selectors are flat capsules with one squared end, stacked in coloured blocks like console keys.
design_direction.archetype: Consumer messaging app landing: hero with product shot and console-key CTAs, three features, testimonials, three pricing tiers, demo CTA.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Console blink: telemetry numbers tick on a 1.2s interval, elbow bars slide in from the left on load (transform only), CTA capsules flash lighter on press. A 'transmitting' amber dot pulses beside the demo CTA. All motion disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Left: huge condensed uppercase h1 in ink, sub in body, two capsule CTAs (amber primary 'Open a channel', lavender secondary 'Open the demo'). Right: hero photo inside an elbow frame with telemetry codes on the bezel. Top: an amber elbow bar spanning the page with the product name and a live stardate readout.

images.rationale: Hero used: the console style frames one photo well and the joke (a grown man in a velour tunic reading a group chat at night) lands visually. Demo assets skipped as separate images: the chat demo reuses the three testimonial headshots as member avatars, other members get CSS initial chips. Remaining budget on 3 testimonial headshots.

items.prompt: Editorial photograph, cinematic and deadpan. A middle-aged man sits alone at a small kitchen table at night in a dark apartment, wearing a homemade mustard-amber velour tunic with a black collar, staring with total seriousness at a smartphone held in both hands. Warm amber glow #FF9D3D from the phone, cool lavender #A79BFF rim light from a window, deep space-navy shadows #0B0D1A. Shallow depth of field, 35mm film grain. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no insignia, no rendered UI screens, phone screen faces away.
